newsitem.title: UK: Sharp build seen for 1996/97 sugar stocks - Licht.
newsitem.headline: Sharp build seen for 1996/97 sugar stocks - Licht.

text.p: World sugar stocks could see a sharper build-up this crop year than in 1995/96 as production is set to rise in major exporting nations, the managing director of German statistician F.O. Licht said on Friday.

"Taking into account all the developments to date it looks as if world production in September/August 1996/97 will not show the needed decline to bring production and consumption into line, which means that there will be another addition to stocks," Helmut Ahlfeld told a two-day London conference.
"The problem is that production is expected to grow mainly in the large exporting nations, while last year the bulk was in India, which had only a limited impact on prices," he said.
In October, Licht estimated world production at 123.95 million tonnes for 1996/97, after a previous 125.54 million.
Ahlfeld said the 1996/97 crop year began with surplus sugar stocks of roughly nine million tonnes, although most of this was locked up in India.

The October forecast estimated surplus stocks could rise to six million tonnes this crop year. The growth in stocks was likely to continue into 1996/97 on account of the expected end of negative growth in eastern Europe, abundant supplies in developing countries and slower growth in demand for high fructose corn syrup (HFCS).
"This augurs ill for the further development of world prices and it would not come as a surprise if the market were to remain under pressure throughout 1996/97," Ahlfeld said.
